category_info.bloom_season: late spring through autumn, peaking in early summer
category_info.bloom_cycle: repeat-flowering in modern varieties; old garden roses often bloom once per year
category_info.deadheading: cut spent blooms just above the first 5-leaflet leaf to encourage new flowering
category_info.vase_life: 5-10 days if cut in the morning at bud stage and placed in clean water
category_info.fertilizer: balanced rose feed in spring after pruning, then after each flush; stop feeding 6 weeks before first frost
category_info.watering_need: deep soak 2-3 times per week at the base; avoid overhead watering

observations.symptom: White powdery coating on young leaves and flower buds
observations.location: New growth at the shoot tips
observations.evidence: Dust-like white film spreading across the upper surface of the youngest leaves

observations.symptom: Slight leaf curling on affected shoots
observations.location: Same young foliage carrying the white film
observations.evidence: Leaf edges curl upward on the shoots where the coating is densest

possible_causes.name: Powdery mildew (Podosphaera pannosa)
possible_causes.reason: White talc-like coating on young rose foliage and buds is the classic symptom of rose powdery mildew

possible_causes.name: Early-stage botrytis on buds
possible_causes.reason: Bud damage can resemble mildew, but botrytis is usually grey-brown and mushy rather than powdery white

recommended_actions.action: Improve airflow: space plants, thin crowded interior stems, and water at the base in the morning
recommended_actions.reason: Powdery mildew thrives on humid, still foliage; drier leaves slow it without chemicals

recommended_actions.action: Prune out the worst-affected tips and dispose of them in household waste
recommended_actions.reason: Removes the largest source of spores and encourages clean new shoots

recommended_actions.action: If it spreads despite the above, ask a nursery for a low-toxicity powdery-mildew option approved for roses
recommended_actions.reason: Local experts can suggest treatments suitable for your region and variety

seasonal_context: Mild dry days with humid nights favor mildew outbreaks in late spring and early summer.
what_to_monitor: Whether new leaves emerge clean after airflow improves
Bud distortion or failed blooming on heavily coated stems
limitations: Powdery mildew species cannot be identified to rose variety from a photo
Other leaf coating look-alikes (e.g. pesticide residue) cannot be excluded without closer inspection
follow_up_questions: Are the plants crowded against a wall or under cover where air stagnates?
Have you noticed the white dust on any neighboring plants?
